# Synthetic data

**All SahiSupply data is synthetic.** It is generated by `backend/app/data/generator.py` with a fixed seed
(42 by default) and never represents a real company, outlet or result.

## What is generated (per industry module)

| Entity | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Warehouses | 5 | Real Maharashtra city coordinates (Bhiwandi, Pune, Nashik, Chh. Sambhajinagar, Nagpur); outbound capacity in litres; cold-storage flag |
| Outlets | 12 | 3 regions (Mumbai Metro, Western Maharashtra, Vidarbha-Marathwada); receiving and cold capacity (0 at some); storage capabilities |
| Products | 15 | Volume, storage class, shelf life, unit cost / price / gross margin. Pharmacy: 5 critical, 4 at 2-8 °C |
| Batches | ~135 | Each product at 3 of 5 warehouses (always incl. hub W2), 2-4 batches each, staggered expiry (~20% short-dated) |
| Routes | 60 | Every warehouse x outlet. Distance = haversine x 1.3 (**straight line, not a road route**); lead time = 1 + floor(km / 350) days; cost per litre = 0.8 + 0.006 x km; capacity in litres; open flag |
| Demand history | 32,400 | 12 outlets x 15 products x 180 days |
| Open orders | 180 | Grocery only: one week drawn from the same demand model (x U(0.95, 1.15)) |
| Outlet on-hand | 180 | One stock record per outlet-product with an expiry date |

## Demand model

```
mu(d,p,t) = scale_d * base_p * mix(d,p) * weekday(t) * trend_p(t) * promo(p,t) * festival(t)
demand    ~ NegativeBinomial(mean = mu, dispersion = 6)
```

* weekday factors differ per industry (e.g. pharmacy low on Sundays, food high at weekends);
* 2-4 promotion windows per product (uplift 1.1-1.6 depending on the industry), known in advance;
* an approximate 2026 festival calendar (Eid, Ganesh Chaturthi, Navratri, Dussehra, Diwali);
* in grocery/food, outlets without a chiller sell only 15% of the normal chilled-product demand.

Because `mu` is known, the forecast backtest reports a **noise floor**: the error a forecaster would have
if it knew the true expected demand. This exists only because the data is synthetic.

## Contested-supply pattern (switchable)

With the pattern **on**, remote outlets (D9-D12, Vidarbha-Marathwada) can only be served from the hub W2,
which is also the cheapest source for nearby urban outlets. That is exactly where warehouse-by-warehouse
greedy planning fails. With the pattern **off**, every route is open. Only routes differ between the two;
every other entity is identical (tested). Every outcome KPI is reported for both (`validation/results.md`).

## Reproducibility

* Same seed -> byte-identical data: the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON is tested in `tests/test_data.py`.
* `python -m scripts.seed_database` loads both route variants into MongoDB (idempotent).
* `python -m scripts.export_snapshot` writes gzipped JSON snapshots and a hash manifest to `data/snapshots/`.
* If MongoDB is down, the API regenerates the same seed-42 data in memory and labels every response
  `data_source: "snapshot"`; runs are then not persisted and the UI says so.
